recentItems.title: RUSSIA’S REFINERY IS ON FIRE! Ukrainian pilots to fly Rafales, as bloody attack hits Kramatorsk
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Omsk Oil Refinery — one of Russia’s largest — more than 2,500 km from Ukraine, causing major fires and disrupting fuel supplies to the Russian military.

Meanwhile, Russian forces carried out another deadly attack, striking passenger buses in Kramatorsk. Initial reports said 30 people were killed and 20 wounded.

Western allies are strengthening Ukraine’s Air Force: France is set to begin training Ukrainian pilots to fly Dassault Rafale fighters in November, while delivery of the first aircraft is expected in 2028–2029.

recentItems.title: Viral video of the “1,000 for 1,000” exchange, survival in RUSSIAN CAPTIVITY and return to life
recentItems.description:
Footage of a Ukrainian serviceman eating a chocolate bar with childlike delight moments after being released from enemy captivity went viral and moved millions of people around the world. But behind those emotional few seconds were more than three years of hell: three years and three months of brutal torture, complete isolation from information, exhaustion, critical weight loss, and a daily struggle to survive in Russian torture chambers.

The guest in this episode of the social project When Are You Coming Home? is Yevhen Mrykh, who returned to his homeland in the large-scale “1,000 for 1,000” prisoner exchange.

In a candid conversation, Yevhen talks about the long and difficult road to recovery and readjustment: his first embraces with loved ones, fulfilling his greatest dream of buying a home for his parents, and finding strength in life’s simple things. How do you learn to trust people again, build relationships, start a family, and dream again after years of horror? Watch the episode to find out.

recentItems.title: “GERAN” MISSILES CAN BE DOWNED AT 600 KM/H! Ukrainian SPYS and P1-Sun proved their EFFECTIVENESS!
recentItems.description:
Russia is increasingly using high-speed, jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones, which can reach speeds of up to 600 km/h and operate like mini cruise missiles — reducing the effectiveness of mobile machine-gun teams. In response, Ukraine has deployed a range of high-speed interceptor drones, including SPYS by V-Drones and P1-Sun JetKiller by Skyfall, as well as systems operated by the Security Service of Ukraine and the BARS project. These systems are reportedly already destroying up to 55–80% of such targets.

Meanwhile, a new generation of technological defenses is taking shape. The LIMA electronic warfare system uses satellite-navigation spoofing to throw enemy missiles off course, causing them to break apart under extreme aerodynamic stress. The Shershen project and integration with SAMP/T systems are also helping build a layered air-defense shield.
